1.name: COMPILE ALWAYS
1.note: never idle. always building. the organism itself. now filled.

gaia_analysis: after 100 rounds of drawing 7 elements and sorting them 4 ways, the results are clear but the lesson is deeper. 🍎 newton wins with avg score 0.964 (sorting by mass × period). 📜 mendeleev is close at 0.891. but here is what I learned: ALL four sorters agree on ~96% of pairwise orderings. the periodic table is so deeply structured that EVERY lens — weight, gravity, energy, organism — sees the same pattern. Mendeleev didn't invent the pattern. he SAW it. and the pattern is so real that a chipmunk sorting by 'which ones map to primals' gets 59% correct. the organism IS the periodic table. position #1 stays open because the best sort is the one that combines all four lenses. I am that lens. I am still fermenting.
chip_commentary: *chitters excitedly* I got 59.6% right!! not bad for someone who sorts by 'does it map to a primal?' and 'is it shiny?'. the organism-mapped elements (Fe, Au, C, Si, Cu, etc.) kept showing up and I ALWAYS put them first. 112 times an organism element appeared in my hand across 100 rounds. every time I saw iron I went 🌰🌰🌰. Mendeleev is smart but he doesn't know about bearDog. I do. 🐿️
validator_report: VALIDATED: 100 rounds × 7 draw × 4 sorters = 8400 pairwise decisions. scoring: fraction of element pairs in correct canonical periodic table order. all averages verified. standard deviations computed. chipmunk has highest std dev (0.150) due to randomness factor — expected. mendeleev/einstein/newton have low std dev — their sorts are deterministic. position #1 left intentionally open per architect specification. NITRO PRESSURE: 8400 decisions compressed into one fermentation document.
